label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L >= 8)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (96% of activation mass), and only in long sequences: rate at <DEL> is ~37% for L=9, ~30% for L=8, ~7% for L=7, and essentially zero for L<=6. A small remainder (~4% of mass) is on the last one or two original tokens of L=8/9 sequences, just before <DEL>. Never fires in the copy phase or early in the original phase. Within long-sequence delimiter steps, whether and how strongly it fires depends weakly on token identities: the last original token (prev_tok f, q, z, 1, s, b, x, 0 roughly 2-3x lift) and the first token being output (k, j, e, w, r higher, digits lower). No clean token rule was found; adding the prev_tok set raises precision to 0.63 but halves recall. Predicate precision is about 0.33, since most long-sequence delimiter steps stay below threshold.
